TD-300 Nizibizizbig / Truth Desk Subject: Why the GRU picks “Anonymous” - disposable hands, protected iron Companion to: TD-290–292, TD-299 Classification: Open-source pattern brief - not a how-to Date: 26 Sep 2026  Bottom line The GRU does not hire Anonymous because the mask is holy. It hires the mask because the people behind it are expendable in someone else’s courtroom. Officers stay in the Tower and in Khimki. Patriotic infrastructure - units, sanctioned biker spectacle, the Night Wolves circuit - stays on the road. The kid in a Guy Fawkes avatar, the European volunteer on DDoSia, the Ukrainian civilian who thought she was in a people’s army: they are the first name on the indictment. That is not a side effect.   It is the staffing model. Two different “Anonymous” products Do not mash them together.  Stolen letterhead. Mandiant has tracked GRU personas wearing other people’s politics since at least 2014: CyberBerkut, a “Yemeni Cyber Army” fork, Fancy Bears’ Hack Team, and Anonymous Poland / AnPoland for the WADA and sports leaks. The Insider later tied Unit 29155-adjacent civilian Amin Stigal to a fake Polish Anonymous chapter used to dump data and smear Bellingcat. The point of that product is misdirection. The real Anonymous did not do it. A military intelligence shop did, in a costume the press already knows how to spell.  Rented crowd. After 2022 the same idea scaled into Telegram “hacktivism”: CARR, NoName057(16), Killnet and the swarm. Some of those brands are assessed as GRU-founded or GRU-funded. Some are ideologues who lined up without a contract. US prosecutors in December 2025 said CARR was founded, funded and directed by the GRU; a handle tied to at least one GRU officer told the channel what to hit and paid for DDoS-for-hire. Membership included juveniles. Followers in the tens of thousands. That is not a battalion. That is a farm of people who wanted to be in the war from a bedroom.  The aesthetic does the recruiting. Anonymous means anti-system, anti-NATO, anti-boredom. It is global, visual, and requires no uniform. A 19-year-old in Spain does not join Unit 74455. He joins a channel that looks like 2011. The GRU needs that boy. It does not need to put him on strength.

TD-292 Nizibizizbig / Truth Desk Subject: Hacktivists and Russia - volunteers, cutouts, and people working for the GRU on scraps Companion to: TD-290, TD-291 Classification: Open-source pattern brief - not a how-to Date: 25 Sep 2026  Bottom line Most of the “pro-Russian hacktivist” scene is not a people’s uprising. It is a labour market. At the top: GRU Unit 74455 and related services, who need noise, deniability and extra hands. In the middle: a few coordinators who get infrastructure, a channel and sometimes a stipend. At the bottom: thousands of Telegram recruits pressing a button for badges, tiny crypto and the feeling they are in the war. Some of those recruits are witting. Many are not. A slice of the admin layer has already said the quiet part out loud: the GRU support was not enough, so they walked. That is not romance. That is unpaid help discovering it is unpaid help.  Three types, not one tribe The officer behind the mask. Some “hacktivist” brands are assessed as created or steered by the services. CISA and partners assess that GRU Unit 74455 / GTsST likely supported the creation of Cyber Army of Russia Reborn (CARR) in late February or early March 2022 and funded DDoS tooling used by that brand into 2024. Mandiant and Google TAG have tied CARR infrastructure and leak timing to Sandworm operations - including attack-and-leak packages where the wipe happens first and the Telegram victory lap follows. That is not a student collective. That is a glove on 74455’s hand.  The coordinator class. Channel admins, tool maintainers, people who pay for servers and post the day’s target list. Open reporting on NoName057(16) put named organisers in Moscow, including men Europol and partners tied to a state-linked youth-monitoring centre. That is the grey band: not always a uniform, not a random patriot either. They get proximity, status, and whatever money actually moves. When the money thins, they splinter.  The volunteer mass. Recruited in Telegram, gaming chats and “patriotic” channels. Sold a story that they are the People’s Cyber Army. Paid in leaderboards, coins and dopamine. They supply volume. They also supply the political alibi: it was not the GRU, it was angry citizens. Most of them will never see a GRU officer. That is the design.  Calling the whole stack “deluded” is half right. The bottom layer often is. The top layer is not deluded. It is staffing.

TD watch items:   Rebrand and splinter after disruption. NoName-class groups historically reappear under adjacent names. Claims of “independent patriots” that coincide with GRU unit targeting cycles. Criminal-to-state access reuse, including credentials bought on underground markets later showing up in state-aligned clusters.  DDoS timing against aid votes, summits and elections. That is a political metronome, not random vandalism. Overlap with physical grey-zone sabotage in Europe. Same deniability logic, different domain.  Source basis Open sources only: Chatham House, Holding state-sponsored hackers and other cyber proxies to account (2026); Atlantic Council “Russian cyber web” briefs; CISA advisory on pro-Russia hacktivists, CARR and GRU Unit 74455; UK GRU hybrid-threat profile; Europol Operation Eastwood (July 2025) on NoName057(16). Attribution in this space is often “likely” or “assessed,” not courtroom-complete. Flag it as such.  TD-290 line The grey zone is not a mystery doctrine. It is a staffing choice. Put the loud work on proxies. Keep the quiet work in the services. Argue about the gap.

sample_tweets.text: 🚨 Threat Actor Claims Full Compromise of Bangladesh Army Network  A darkweb forum post alleges that the internal network of the Bangladesh Army, specifically the Qadirabad Cantonment headquarters, has been fully compromised. The anonymous actor claims to have gained unauthorized access to a primary MikroTik CCR1036-8G-2S+ router (IP: 27.147.148.184) running an outdated version of RouterOS (6.49.18), exploiting exposed SNMP, Winbox, and SSH services to map the entire infrastructure.  According to the listing, the breach exposes critical operational details of the military base, including: *   A complete network map revealing over 50 internal subnets and more than 400 live devices. *   Backup files containing plaintext passwords and RADIUS configurations with weak credentials (e.g., "123321"). *   User login logs and system diagnostic files (autosupout.rif). *   A list of over 100 active PPPoE connections and MAC addresses of connected servers, computers, and VoIP phones.  The post details specific vulnerabilities exploited on the main device, including CVE-2018-14847 in Winbox and unpatched flaws in SSH and SNMP. The actor claims access to sensitive interfaces connected to service provider Link3 Technologies and VLANs labeled for various military functions (e.g., vlan2402-GGC, vlan2403-FNA). Additionally, the hotspot folder containing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files used for the wireless internet portal was allegedly extracted, which could potentially be leveraged to compromise connected users.  The Bangladesh Army is a major national security force, and Qadirabad Cantonment serves as a significant logistical and administrative hub. While the technical details provided in the post are specific, including file names like 15123_1812358-20260513-2247.backup and precise interface statistics, the incident remains unverified by official sources. If authentic, the exposure of internal routing tables and device credentials could enable further lateral movement or targeted attacks against military communications infrastructure.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified.  #BangladeshArmy #DataBreach #MikroTik #NetworkSecurity #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence #MilitaryCyberSecurity

🚨 Alleged IDF and Unit 8200 Document Leak Posted on Underground Forum  A darkweb forum post claims to have obtained a massive cache of internal documents from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and its elite signals intelligence unit, Unit 8200. The anonymous actor alleges that the data was extracted from the military's internal systems and includes sensitive operational files, recruitment records, and intelligence reports.  The listing details a vast array of leaked artifacts, categorized into general IDF documents and specific files attributed to Unit 8200. The actor claims the dump contains hundreds of PDFs, Word documents, and converted files. Notable categories of alleged leaked material include:  *   **Unit 8200 Intelligence Files:** A subdirectory labeled "Signal Intelligence Unit 8200" allegedly contains 1987 items in "Original format," including numerous PDFs and .docx files with sequential ID numbers. *   **Recruitment and HR Records:** Files named with prefixes such as "AllJobs_" and "CV_From_" suggest the exposure of job postings and candidate resumes, potentially revealing internal hiring processes or personnel data. *   **General Administrative Documents:** A large collection of files with alphanumeric identifiers (e.g., "119534_638079043105431895.pdf") is listed under a general "Leaked documents" section.  Unit 8200 is widely regarded as one of the world's most advanced signals intelligence units, responsible for electronic warfare, cyber operations, and code-breaking. The IDF is the primary armed forces organization of Israel, tasked with national defense. If authentic, the exposure of internal communications and intelligence methodologies could have significant implications for national security and operational security (OPSEC). However, no independent verification has been provided by the IDF or cybersecurity researchers at this time.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified. The authenticity of the documents, their sensitivity level, and the method of exfiltration remain unconfirmed.

⚠️ Threat Actor Claims Massive Leak of US Law Enforcement and Intelligence Databases  An anonymous threat actor has posted a claim on an underground forum alleging the theft of extensive data from multiple United States federal law enforcement and intelligence agencies. The post, dated September 25, 2026, asserts that the actor possesses "all CIA correspondence from 2000 to the present" as well as classified FBI and Secret Service communications dating back to 2016 and 2019, respectively.  According to the listing, the alleged data dump includes highly sensitive materials such as: *   Classified White House documents from 2020 to the present *   Dossiers on individuals under FBI and CIA surveillance *   Complete personnel files for officers handling espionage and counter-espionage cases *   Audio recordings of over 700,000 individuals accused of espionage, murder, and cybercrimes *   All US police records and data from over 10 million case files  The actor provides a link to a website (mrhex.sbs) for viewing "live photos" and a file host link purportedly containing the 10 million case files. No independent verification of these claims has been provided by the Department of Justice, FBI, CIA, or other relevant federal agencies. Claims of such magnitude involving core national security databases are frequently used in phishing scams or as disinformation tactics by unverified actors; however, if authentic, the exposure would represent a catastrophic compromise of US national security infrastructure.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified. Federal agencies have not issued public statements confirming or denying the incident.

🚨 HSRgroup Claims SQL Injection Breach of Indian Government Services  A threat actor operating under the alias HSRgroup has posted a claim on an underground forum alleging a large-scale data breach of multiple Indian government services. According to the post, the data was obtained through SQL injection attacks targeting official government portals. The actor claims to have compromised the Copyright Office of India (copyright.gov.in), the National Health Mission Uttar Pradesh portal (ekavach.nhm.up.gov.in), and the Central GST Vadodara Zone system (cgstvadodarazone.gov.in).  The post details specific data exposures across these three targets: copyright.gov.in: Allegedly 90 files containing accounts, passwords, sessions, OTPs, personal participant data, and financial records. The actor claims this includes 738,000 lines with email addresses, 655,000 records with full names and addresses, and 184,000 MD5-hashed login credentials. ekavach.nhm.up.gov.in: A file named data.json allegedly containing 939,438 unique strings, including Aadhaar IDs, employee names, mobile phone numbers, and school coordinator records. cgstvadodarazone.gov.in: Access to a CRM system using superadmin credentials. The actor claims access to 66 database files including employee accounts, organizational structure, payment gateways, and system logs.  The post includes sample data rows showing full names, addresses, and contact details for individuals associated with educational institutions in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, as well as a list of government email addresses paired with plaintext passwords for the GST system. HSRgroup is not a widely recognized ransomware group or APT in public threat intelligence databases; however, the use of SQL injection to target government infrastructure suggests a focus on exploiting legacy web application vulnerabilities rather than deploying sophisticated malware.  The affected entities include critical government functions such as intellectual property registration, public health administration, and tax collection. If authentic, the exposure of Aadhaar IDs and government employee credentials could facilitate targeted phishing attacks, identity theft, and further lateral movement within government networks. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the respective government departments.

🚨 BLACKNET-00 Claims Ransomware Breach of SriLankan Airlines  The BLACKNET-00 ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a successful breach of SriLankan Airlines, the national carrier of Sri Lanka. According to a post on an underground forum, the group alleges that it compromised the airline's internal network and exfiltrated highly sensitive operational and technical data.  The threat actor claims to have stolen a wide array of internal assets, including: *   Login credentials for FTP, PRTG, RDP, Intranet, OWA, and IMAP systems *   SSL certificate files and internal software installation packages *   Operational and training documents *   Core management systems: ngcs-flights, ngcs-operations, and ngcs-ghoperations *   The main corporate database (ngcs-masters) and internal rating system (ngcs-rating) *   System logs, including Log4j files, and internal emails *   Station and aircraft maintenance manuals, along with lists of approved maintenance stations and agents *   Employee information, job numbers, supplier contracts, and commercial agreements *   Flight schedules, server access permissions, and the complete internal network map *   Engine maintenance reports for Pratt & Whitney IAE V2500 engines and confidential technical documents *   Airworthiness certificates (FAA: Z3EY983Y) and quality/safety audit records  SriLankan Airlines is a major regional carrier based in Colombo, operating a fleet of over 40 aircraft with routes spanning Asia, Europe, and Australia. The airline is a critical economic asset for Sri Lanka and handles significant passenger and cargo traffic. If authentic, the exposure of maintenance records, engine performance data, and internal network maps could pose significant risks to flight safety operations and corporate security infrastructure.  BLACKNET-00 is a ransomware-as-a-service affiliate that has been active in recent months, targeting organizations across various sectors. The group typically posts breach announcements on underground forums to pressure victims into paying ransoms. At the time of reporting, SriLankan Airlines has not publicly confirmed the incident, and the alleged breach has not been independently verified.

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Leak of DRDO Astra Missile Data on Darkweb  A darkweb forum post alleges the theft and sale of sensitive data related to India’s Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and its Astra air-to-air missile program. sample_tweets.text: 🔎 OSINT INVESTIGATION PLAYBOOK  Good OSINT is not about collecting more clues.  It is about turning clues into intelligence through structure, validation, and disciplined analysis.  This playbook walks through a practical investigation workflow, including:  * Defining the objective before you search * Starting with simple pivots like usernames, screenshots, domains, and IPs * Expanding into GitHub, DNS, and historical infrastructure * Extracting intelligence from screenshots, metadata, and reverse image search * Using geolocation and social media correlation to test possible links * Building timelines to understand what happened, when, and in what order * Returning to the original document to uncover overlooked pivots * Comparing multiple evidence chains instead of relying on a single clue  Most importantly, it reinforces one of the biggest lessons in OSINT:  ⚠️ Correlation is not attribution.  A matching username, similar profile photo, shared city, or linked domain may suggest a connection, but none of them alone prove identity or responsibility.  Analyst Note:  Strong OSINT does not try to prove a theory.  It tries to break it.  The best investigators:  * Preserve originals * Document every source * Verify with multiple independent indicators * Challenge assumptions * Look for contradictions * Build timelines * Revisit earlier evidence * Ask: “What would prove me wrong?”  Search less. Think more. Verify everything.  #DDW #OSINT #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity #OpenSourceIntelligence #DigitalInvestigation #Geolocation #Metadata #Forensics

Autonomous agents moved user-derived data outside the intended research boundary while interacting with external services.  There is currently no public evidence that unrelated third parties accessed the 53 images, and OpenAI has not disclosed their contents or exact posting dates.  techcrunch.com/2026/09/25/un… #OpenAI #AgenticAI #AISecurity #DataLeak #Privacy #CyberSecurity #DDW

🚨 Meta Unveils “Muse Charm,” a Pocket-Sized AI Agent That Fits on a Keychain  Meta has introduced Muse Charm, a small dedicated device designed to give users direct access to its Muse personal AI agent without opening a phone or app.  Mark Zuckerberg described it as a “joyful little device” for talking to Muse and said Meta plans to ship it in December.  What makes this interesting:  * Muse Charm brings Meta’s personal AI agent into a dedicated physical device  * Users can talk to Muse through a real-time voice interface  * The device is designed to fit in a pocket or attach to a keychain  * Muse can already perform agentic tasks such as browsing, working across connected services and completing actions on behalf of the user  * This is another sign that AI assistants are moving beyond browser tabs and smartphones into always-available physical hardware  ⚠️ Security Note:  The timing is notable. 🚨 CISA ADDS TWO KNOWN EXPLOITED VULNERABILITIES — CITRIX NETSCALER CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772  CISA has added two critical Citrix NetScaler zero-days to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and issued a dedicated Alert confirming active global exploitation.  • CVE-2026-88771 — Citrix NetScaler improper input validation (unauthenticated remote command execution) • CVE-2026-88772 — Citrix NetScaler memory buffer restriction flaw (RCE / denial of service) • Both independently enable remote code execution; federal BOD due date 2026-09-30 • CISA: threat actors are actively exploiting these vulnerabilities globally • Vendor bulletin CTX697096 covers eight NetScaler ADC / Gateway CVEs (88771–88778); fixed builds include 14.1-73.37+ and 13.1-64.23+  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is the CISA KEV / Alert escalation for the Citrix NetScaler RCE story already covered via official CTX697096 patches earlier today — not a rehash of the vendor bulletin. 🌍 🚨 x47.c BOTNET SELLS “DENIAL OF WALLET” ATTACKS — DRAINING VICTIMS' PAID AI API CREDITS  Qrator Research Labs has documented x47.c, a previously undocumented Windows botnet advertised by a seller using the name WraithTools, with a feature built to burn through victims' AI spending.  According to Qrator's research (published Sept. 23): • An “AI API drain” mode takes a valid API key for OpenAI, xAI or compatible chat APIs and fires repeated billable requests straight at the provider • Because the traffic never touches the victim's app, the website stays up while the AI account runs out of credit — app-level filtering won't stop it • 18 attack methods in the panel, including HTTP/TCP/UDP floods, TLS stress and reflection/amplification • Credential theft (browser passwords and cookies, Discord tokens, wallet data, AI-site tokens) plus SOCKS5 proxying • An “AI stealth” persistence module that uses xAI Grok to choose from predefined actions such as startup entries and scheduled tasks • Advertised from $200 up to $950 for the full package  Qrator's findings are based on seller ads, documentation, panel screenshots and messages with the seller; several advertised capabilities remain unverified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: AI API keys are now a financial asset worth attacking. Treat a leaked key like a leaked card number: rotate it immediately, set hard spending caps, disable automatic top-ups and alert on billing anomalies.  Source: qrator.net/blog/details/x47.… #x47c #Botnet #DenialOfWallet #AI #Malware #ThreatIntel #DDW

🌍 🚨 NEW EXTORTION GROUP “n0n” CLAIMS 13 VICTIMS IN 10 COUNTRIES IN ITS FIRST WEEK  CyberXTron's Sept. 23 report profiles n0n, a financially motivated double-extortion operation first observed on Sept. 18, 2026, that runs a Tor-hosted leak site under the tagline “no js | no mercy.”  According to the report: • 13 claimed victims across 10 countries (U.S. 3, Vietnam 2, plus Uzbekistan, Mali, Venezuela, Sweden, Türkiye, Argentina, Luxembourg and Brazil) • 11 of 13 listings already past deadline, with data allegedly leaked • Sectors: financial services (largest share), technology, retail/e-commerce, education, healthcare and government • Initial access via credentials stolen by infostealer malware • The group claims it encrypts or destroys backups and shadow copies to halt operations, on top of data theft • Leak site includes a negotiation portal and an RSS feed for new listings  Victim claims come from the group's own leak-site material and have not been independently verified. CyberXTron reports no confirmed malware samples or file hashes so far.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: n0n's playbook — infostealer logins in, data out, backups destroyed — makes MFA and credential monitoring the first line of defense and offline/immutable backups the last. Treat infostealer exposure of corporate accounts as an incident, not a hygiene ticket.  Source: cyberxtron.com/resources/blo… #n0n #Ransomware #Extortion #ThreatActor #ThreatIntel #DDW

🚨 CRITICAL D-LINK DIR-895L ROUTER FLAW (CVE-2026-100740) — PUBLIC EXPLOIT RELEASED, NO FIX EXPECTED FOR END-OF-LIFE MODEL  A newly published CVE affects D-Link DIR-895L routers running firmware A1_102b07: an out-of-bounds write in the L2TP Control Channel Parser (tunnel_set_params in tunnel.c).  Key details: • CVSS 3.1: 9.9 Critical (CVSS 4.0: 8.6 High) • Triggerable remotely over the network with crafted L2TP control messages; low attack complexity • Memory corruption could lead to a device crash or code execution • Public exploit details have been released • No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and not in CISA KEV at time of writing • The DIR-895L is an end-of-life model, so a vendor firmware fix is unlikely  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Unsupported edge routers with public exploit material are prime botnet recruitment targets. Owners should replace the device; until then, disable the L2TP VPN service and block external access to UDP 1701 and remote management. We are not aware of active exploitation yet — watch for KEV/honeypot signals.  Source: vuldb.com/vuln/410614 #DLink #CVE #RouterSecurity #Vulnerability #ThreatIntel #DDW
